corrected_actionable_findings.topic: Direct SDK BOOL success must not be truncated to AL
corrected_actionable_findings.regression: core valid success BOOL0x100 after actual critical-section initialization, followed by complete close

findings.conclusion: DomainStorage owns one runtime/error/heap/FLS/initial-locale graph. Reverse destruction keeps Seed/exception backing, heap providers, ImageState and lock storage alive through FLS Binding destruction.
The one-time ErrorProxy and Invalid policy links bind after the exact FLS Binding exists and before any initialization. No unbound-success fallback or second outer CRT initialization is added.

Independent audit found low-byte truncation of direct SDK BOOL success in lock initialization. Root corrected the full-result test; a real initialized critical section returning legal BOOL 0x100 now initializes and closes successfully in the core regression.

Only ACRT locks 0/4/5 are initialized. Normal FALSE failure cleans up the completed prefix in reverse order; successful current lock is counted before later failures. Native SDK callbacks retain their declared nonthrowing outcome precondition.

Every ThreadDomain route uses binding.state(), not a copied index/state. Normal allocation/publication failures release the slot and heap prefix. Failed native release remains distinct from the source-invalidated index.

First close invokes recovered uninitialize once and preserves a failed native slot. Later close calls retry_release without silently repeating source cleanup. Data, heap and locks remain retained until actual release succeeds.

Unknown exception during published PTD construction poisons the owner rather than fabricating rollback of partial lock/reference effects. Unknown native module load/release outcome similarly preserves its ticket and prevents successful close.

make_threads calls the actual B5 make_recovered_threads factory with the same runtime/errors/PTD/heap/invalid objects. Its shared provider anchor owns DomainStorage without a strong self-cycle. close returns false while a provider remains alive.

B3/B4 must stop admission, join all workers and their FLS callbacks, and drain application cleanup before Runtime/provider destruction. Provider destruction releases the anchor; only then may DomainStorage release main/domain FLS and modules.

InitialLocale owns relocated ImageState and actual LONG/Interlocked counters. Existing source locale-reference bodies are reused under actual owned ACRT4/5 locks. Foreign/dynamic locale/MB access and deep free are rejected rather than advertised as supported.

New/invalid callbacks are explicitly selected rebuilt callback ABIs and coherent cookie encodings. No selected invalid callback resolves to the explicit compiler abort policy; this does not reconstruct native MSVC Watson/EH behavior.

NativeRuntime reserves stable per-load reference tickets before native loading, including duplicate HMODULE values. Release consumes only successful prefixes and retains failures for retry. SDK/foreign calls execute outside the bookkeeping mutex.

Runtime header now explicitly restricts worker-time free_library to extra duplicate refs while an independently retained cache reference keeps code mapped. Last-reference release is serialized with all lookups/RO calls and occurs only at whole-domain quiescence. Ownership checks are not per-procedure lifetime leases.

Load/procedure/release pointers use exact SDK types. RO calls use actual decltype SDK callback types. AppPolicy output bits transfer bytewise both ways, including failure, without forged int32_t/enum aliases. Current-process PEB prefix reading is a stated x64 platform boundary.

Captured core PASS168 covers real heap/FLS/locks, normal constructor prefixes, explicit FLS-release retry, module-reference failure prefixes, typed API/source policy paths, actual system-only module loading, unsupported locale rejection and terminal children.

Captured integration PASS101 exercises actual make_recovered_threads/ThreadEffects through three simultaneous own worker PTDs and the full B3/B4 queued bootstrap graph. Heap observations are locked, worker observations use atomics, and shared test counters are not concurrently mutated.

The restricted owned initial-locale worker domain is concretely assembled and exercised. Full mutable/global CRT, original EH/Watson/FILE ABI, foreign providers, general Execution concurrency and PE/image-unload gates remain open. No native body/closure or DLL completion percentage is added.

limits: All control methods and raw PTD/phase/index observations require the original controller or whole-domain quiescence. Borrowed cells/pointers expire before FLS release.

A NativeThreads provider must not be destroyed with pending/suspended/unjoined workers. B3 tracking and caller admission policy establish that precondition; a provider anchor alone is not a worker join.
Native SDK callbacks must obey Win32 nonthrowing outcome contracts. Arbitrary exception/SEH and concurrent OOM/shared fallback-state equivalence are not established.

Initial-locale-only selection is a new explicit source policy; ImageState data is not silently declared a fully initialized original CRT image. Exception identity/backing lifetime is explicit caller input and is not native exception-table ABI proof.
free_library during workers is limited to duplicate-reference release with an independently retained code-mapping reference. The recovered missing-cache/concurrent-unload edge remains unproven.
Containing image must remain mapped through all worker and FLS callbacks regardless of Context module pin. Loader-lock/DLL-unload/PE-entry proof remains separate.

Core policy source tests inject typed API exports; integration explicitly seeds thread_policy=1 to isolate the PTD/heap/lock graph. This is not an observed original or default production policy value.
Compiler abort and selected rebuilt handler ABIs are compatibility policies, not recovered MSVC Watson/EH behavior. Full native CRT-domain equivalence and production DLL readiness remain false.
